actions.name: Use open source scanning tools to find vulnerabilities
actions.description: The threat actors use a variety of open source scanning tools to find vulnerabilities in networks and web-based applications, including BBScan, dirsearch, Fscan, ksubdomain, masscan, NMAP, OneForAll, ShuiZe, and wpscan.

actions.name: Use MicroScan to scan websites for vulnerabilities
actions.description: The threat actors have used a malicious Python-based web application called MicroScan containing over 1,300 penetration testing scripts to scan websites for specific vulnerabilities targeting services including OpenSSL, Oracle WebLogic, Rejetto, WordPress, Juniper ScreenOS, Jenkins, and Apache Struts.

actions.name: Execute cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks
actions.description: The threat actors have used JavaScript and HTML code to execute cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks on vulnerable websites to modify webpage content and harvest user credentials.

actions.name: Deliver live700_v1.exe malware via XSS payload
actions.description: After executing the XSS payload, the threat actors deliver a password-protected .zip file containing the executable live700_v1.exe, which runs a process named DiagTrack.exe and establishes encrypted communications with the domain dns.studiocloud.xyz to likely exfiltrate user email data.

actions.name: Use EBurst tool for password spraying and guessing on Microsoft Exchange servers
actions.description: The threat actors use EBurst, an open source Python-based tool, to target Microsoft Office365 Cloud environment accounts by performing password spraying and password guessing against multiple interfaces of Microsoft Exchange servers.

actions.name: Install SoftEther VPN software clients for persistence
actions.description: The threat actors install SoftEther VPN software clients on victim devices to establish persistence and obfuscate command and control communications, often downloading installers named conhost.exe or dllhost.exe using PowerShell or LOTL binaries on Windows, or curl/wget on Linux/Unix.

actions.name: Use PHP script Curlc4.txt to obtain emails via Microsoft EWS API
actions.description: The threat actors created a bot using the PHP script Curlc4.txt to interface with the Microsoft Exchange Web Services (EWS) API to access and exfiltrate emails and content items, compressing and sometimes encrypting the data before uploading it to a remote server.
actions.epistemic_reason: 原文以不確定語氣陳述（如 may have／appears to／we believe），不是已確認的事實。

actions.name: Use DC.exe to execute DCSync replication technique
actions.description: The threat actors used DC.exe to perform the DCSync replication technique to copy sensitive information from Active Directory, including account credentials, group membership details, and trust relationships, by binding to the victim’s domain controller via RPC.

actions.name: Use office-cli command-line utility to access and exfiltrate Microsoft Outlook 365 emails
actions.description: The threat actors use office-cli, a Linux-based command-line utility, to continuously target and access Microsoft Outlook 365 email accounts, automating exfiltration of mail content using configuration files containing credentials.

The .zip file’s contents originate from encoded bytes within the XSS payload and contain the executable file live700_v1.exe. evidence.quote: The FBI observed that the threat actors created a bot using the PHP script Curlc4.txt to obtain emails from victims. The script is specifically designed to interface with the Microsoft EWS API, which allows the threat actors to access email and content items, such as calendars and contacts. Based on observations, the script appears to be stand-alone rather than installed on a compromised device. The script uploaded emails to a remote server, obfuscating many of the directories and files it created, and changed the name of the child process to crypto. The script downloaded the original file from https://upl.natcloudservice[.]com using IP address 149.28.132[.]137. The main C2 domain for the bot was natcloudservice[.]com, and the domain communicated with https://natcloudservice[.]com/ews and upl.natcloudservice[.]com/ews. Before exfiltration, the bot compressed emails. In some instances, the threat actor also used a password to encrypt emails using RC4 or AES-128-CBC.
